spatial_disposition.evidence: The Russian State Archives official guides to the office of the Ruler of Priamur Zemsky Krai (https://guides.rusarchives.ru/terms/7/897/pravitel-priamurskogo-zemskogo-kraya-mk-diterihs-g-vladivostok) locate its headquarters in Vladivostok in 1922. The entity was an anti-Bolshevik Far Eastern remnant regime with shifting contested control during the Japanese withdrawal, not the contemporaneous Far Eastern Republic. No verified first-class Place ID, stable 1922 historical border geometry, or authorized spatial display binding is asserted. Keep spatial registration reviewed_hold instead of fabricating territorial ownership.

activity.role: Supreme Ruler of Priamur Zemsky Krai
activity.notes: Mikhail Konstantinovich Diterikhs (1874–1937) assumed supreme political authority over the anti-Bolshevik Priamur Zemsky Krai at Vladivostok on 8 August 1922, under a Zemsky Sobor settlement, and served as the commander/voevoda of the Zemskaya Rat. Russian state archival guides distinguish the former Provisional Priamur Government (founded 1921, ruled by the Merkulov circle) from its 1922 Zemsky Krai reorganization under Diterikhs. This polity is not the Far Eastern Republic, an opposing state whose forces took Vladivostok on 25 October 1922. The 25 October end records the approximate collapse of the regime, not an independently attested resignation hour or claim that Diterikhs personally controlled Vladivostok up to that exact instant. The 1922 regime's monarchist political programme, military defeat and Japanese troop withdrawal are noted; earlier provisional rule from 1921 must not be incorrectly assigned to his reign.
